extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent examiners, and law students studying interference practice
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, standards, and evidentiary criteria governing patent interference proceedings: burden and proof of priority, admissible evidence, procedural requirements for depositions/briefs/motions, grounds and procedure for dissolution, and appeal remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension_of_time_for_evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for taking evidence may be extended upon a motion disclosing under oath the reasons for inability to obtain evidence within prescribed period, the names of witnesses desired, the facts expected to be proved by them, and efforts already made to secure their earlier attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A failure to complete testimony within the period assigned is not permitted to delay the final hearing. Examiner may postpone hearing for sufficient reasons; absent postponement, a later applicant whose evidence was completed may insist on hearing and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: General_rules_of_evidence_apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The general rules of evidence apply in interference cases to the same extent and in the same manner as in the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cited cases (e.g., Millward v. Barnes). Rules of evidence and competency issues are governed by law; technical defects that cause no substantial injury will not be fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority_of_inventive_act
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority consists in prior conception of the idea and prior embodiment of the idea in a practically operative art or reasonable diligence in perfecting such embodiment; successful claimant must establish priority by a clear preponderance of evidence (not necessarily beyond reasonable doubt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must overcome presumptions against claimant arising from earlier applications/patents and affirmatively establish right to priority as against other parties (sufficient to defeat their patents in courts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden_of_proof_against_a_patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimant against a patent has the burden of proof to show prior invention or priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the prima facie proof arising from the patent is outweighed by evidence of prior invention, the burden shifts to the patentee to respond. An applicant in interference with a patent need not prove priority beyond reasonable doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner_rights_on_foreign_patents_and_construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner of interferences has the exclusive right to decide as to competency, construction, scope, and legal meaning of all foreign patents or other evidence, and to determine whether they cover the same invention as in interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office determinations of coverage and meaning are central to interference practice (see Faure v. Bradley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight_of_self-serving_oath_of_invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The assertion by a party that he 'invented' at a certain date is of little weight against contrary facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oaths claiming invention dates must be supported by corroborating evidence; uncorroborated assertions are weak (see Slade v. Blair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint_inventor_presumption_and_oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Where one of two joint patentees applies for a sole patent, he must overcome by evidence the presumption arising from his oath as joint-inventor and the prima facie case presented by the prior patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sworn joint-inventor status creates a presumption against sole rights; must be rebutted by evidence (Lovrien v. Banister).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception_and_reduction_to_practice_evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful claimant must show he first conceived the invention and used reasonable diligence in reducing it to practice; evidence may include verbal descriptions, drawings, sketches, models, equivalent devices, or any other manifestation sufficient for complete expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary statements fix dates; evidence inconsistent with those statements is suspicious. Models/drawings have limited weight unless they show an operative embodiment. Experimental/embryonic descriptions generally insufficient to establish completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary_statement_not_affirmative_evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary statement is not admissible in evidence in favor of the party making it, though it may be used against him as rebutting or limiting his other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original statement and its amendments will be considered in assessing the weight of other evidence about actual dates; statements of belief may be corrected by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign_inventor_date_limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign patentee cannot prove an earlier date for his invention than the date of his foreign patent; a foreign inventor who has not patented abroad cannot use foreign acts to anticipate dates of first knowledge in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a foreign patentee can carry his date back to his foreign patent is doubtful in some circumstances; English specifications' evidentiary value discussed in cases cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroyed_drawings_and_corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: The uncontradicted oath of an applicant that he made drawings at a certain time, if supported by one other credible witness, is sufficient even if the drawings have been destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketches prepared for the occasion have little profit except as illustrations of other evidence; mere descriptions or destroyed drawings are of little weight to show priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devices_equivalent_in_principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Devices produced by the applicant which are equivalent in principle may fix the date of the invention; a machine embracing all features in dispute may serve to show the date even if lacking later improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical embodiments that include disputed features are strong evidence of date of invention (cited cases: Binf v. Walsh, Hockhausen v. Weston).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandoned_experiments_cannot_revive_priority
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned experiment cannot be revived so as to secure priority on interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental reductions that failed to reach consummation cannot defeat a later patent founded on a full invention (Sheridan v. Latus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction_to_practice_requires_operative_art
rubrics_metrics.description: In proving reduction to practice the claimant must establish existence of an operative art or instrument capable of practical employment; models, drawings and descriptions have but little weight on this point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental models illustrating a theory alone are usually insufficient; actual operative embodiment or practical use is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence_in_reduction_to_practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligence in reducing to practice may be shown by any testimony applicable to the peculiar circumstances of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of steps taken (dates, witnesses, efforts) to perfect the embodiment is relevant; failure to show reasonable diligence may defeat claim of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity_of_evidence_to_statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence must conform to the preliminary statement or it will be rejected; any substantial variance between the statement and the evidence renders the evidence suspicious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statement fixes dates by belief, testimony may render them more certain, but substantial contradictions undermine credibility (Hovey v. Dufeland, McCullough v. Watkins).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner_rules_for_taking_testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute authorizes the Commissioner to make rules for taking testimony: evidence in contested cases must be presented as depositions taken upon due notice in the form of interrogatories and replies, sealed and forwarded to the Commissioner; depositions abroad may be taken before an American consul on order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositions returned are subject to inspection but cannot be withdrawn; unless otherwise authorized they must be printed and copies furnished to the Office and contestants. Caveats and printed publications may be filed as evidence with due notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility_dependant_on_proper_procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: No evidence touching matters in dispute can be considered at the hearing unless obtained in accordance with the rules for taking testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical irregularities may be cured by re-taking testimony or other corrective steps; mere procedural defects not causing substantial injury are generally disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable_notice_for_depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice to take testimony must be reasonable; a notice that requires a party to travel night and day is not reasonable notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to appear after reasonable notice operates as a waiver of all technical irregularities (Hoosier Drill Co. v. Ingels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency_of_witnesses_and_spousal_testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses in interferences are under control of the courts; husband and wife are not competent witnesses for or against each other in interference proceedings in some jurisdictions/cases (Marsh v. Rein; contra cases exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competency rules follow general law; check controlling precedent in the relevant district.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions_to_suppress_and_timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to evidence should be raised at the hearing under the rules; it is always better to move to suppress evidence in advance of the hearing, and such motions must be made without unreasonable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deposition improperly taken may be objected to at the interference hearing; a motion to suppress delayed without reasonable excuse may be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences_of_refusal_to_answer_cross_examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a witness in an interference refuses to answer a proper question on cross-examination, his entire testimony will be excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to answer damages credibility and may void the utility of the deposition (Milligan v. Niedringhaus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefs_and_argument_filing_rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments and briefs in all contested cases should be printed and filed before the hearing; parties neglecting this have no right to an extension of time for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the day named for hearing any party appearing will be heard, but no case will be taken up for oral argument after the appointed day except by consent of all parties. After arguments are completed, no further hearing is accorded except by tribunal request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality_and_bases_of_judgment_of_priority
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference cannot be determined without formal dissolution or a judgment on the issue of priority; judgment may be rendered on testimony, on a written concession signed by the parties themselves (not merely attorneys), or on written declaration of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written concessions must be consistent with facts; false or fraudulent admissions are void. Examiner must apply the same rules about inventive performance and completeness as courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption_of_priority_by_filing_order
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are presumed to have made the invention in chronological order of filing their original applications; burden rests on those who seek to establish a different order of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless proof shows otherwise, priority awarded to first filer (with exceptions for reduction to practice and foreign/domestic rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign_vs_domestic_priority_rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where one party is a foreign inventor and others are American, Americans are entitled to priority unless the foreign invention was known/used/patented/published in the U.S. before the Americans' conception; where a foreign patentee has a foreign patent he may prevail over a later U.S. applicant; among foreign patentees earliest foreign patentee has superior right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither party has a foreign patent, the earliest introducer into the U.S. prevails. Rules vary by fact pattern; see cited cases (Lauder v. Crowell and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect_of_no_priority_proved
rubrics_metrics.description: Where neither party proves priority, judgment is rendered against both so that both may be enabled to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defeated claimant still has remedy in equity; a judgment in interference is not final except within the Patent Office—defeated parties may sue by bill in equity under statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolution_of_interference_ground_on_patentability_and_other_bases
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference may be dissolved if its further prosecution is useless; grounds include non-patentability of the invention (want of novelty, lack of utility), absence of rightful party, disclaimer by later applicant, or proof of abandonment (e.g., public use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to dissolve based on patentability must be transmitted to primary examiner; if remanded for want of patentability the interference is dissolved pro hac vice and applications proceed ex parte. Motions must be based on the application alone, not on preliminary statement or outside matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing_for_motions_to_dissolve
rubrics_metrics.description: If a motion to dissolve an interference is not filed within twenty days after the statement is approved, the delay must be explained or the examiner of interferences will not send the case to the primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely move may be appealed to the Commissioner; timely procedural steps are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals_in_interference_proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision of the examiner of interferences is conclusive unless appealed; appeal lies on questions involved in the issue of priority to the examiners-in-chief and then to the Commissioner in person; from the Commissioner there is no further appeal within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be accompanied by a brief stating reasons. The Commissioner, when he hears an interference in person, must consider law and evidence. Remedies after final Office decisions include bills in equity to enforce rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures_and_validity_of_concessions
rubrics_metrics.description: An agreement conceding priority is not good unless signed by the adverse party himself; an attorney has no authority to sign such concession for the client in this context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concessions contrary to truth are void. Concession of priority available only between the parties and only in reference to pending proceedings.
